texts.preamble: Ajay (I)(Fir414/2019/Burari) vs Sanjay Kachhi (Oic) on 9 September, 2024 In The Court Of Dr. Ruchi Aggarwal Asrani Presiding Officer, Mact-01 (Central) Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi. Dlct010007622021 Mact No. : 137/2021 Fir No. : 414/2019 Ps : Burari u/s : 279/337/304A Ipc 1.
texts.facts: The DAR revealed that a Road Traffic Accident took place on 15.12.2019 at about 08:00 PM in front of Nirankari Sant Samagam, Main Road towards Burari Bypass, Delhi wherein the Sh. Pappu had expired and Sh. Ajay sustained simple injury. The accident took place with the vehicle i.e. Ajay (I)(Fir414/2019/Burari) vs Sanjay Kachhi (Oic) on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172781374/ 1 Tractor bearing registration No. HR-55G-3251 driven rashly and negligently by respondent No.1, Sanjay, owned by respondent no. 2, Vichitra Construction Pvt. Ltd. and insured with respondent no. 3, Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Brief facts of the case: 2. Based on the facts outlined in the DAR, it emerges that the information of the accident in question was received at P.S. Burari vide GD No. 6A on 16.12.2019 at 12:41 AM and on receiving the information, ASI Roop Singh along with Ct. Kuldeep went to the LNJP Hospital, where they met with injured persons Pappu and Ajay and collected MLC nos. 113652844/19 and 113692859/19 of injured persons respectively. Injured Ajay refused to give the statement as he was suffering from severe pain. Doctor informed that the injured Pappu was not in a position to give his statement. IO and Ct. Kuldeep went to the spot, where one Tractor bearing no. HR-55G-3251 was found parked at the roadside in an accidental condition. On the basis of MLC of both the inured persons, the offence under Section 279/337 IPC was found to have been committed. Accordingly, FIR was registered. 3. During the course of investigation, IO took the tractor in custody and prepared the site plan. IO received an information that Sh. Pappu had expired. IO reached the hospital, collected the body of Pappu and preserved it in the mortuary of Maulana Azad Medical College, Delhi. Thereafter, offence u/s. 304A IPC was added. 4. During further course of investigation, postmortem of the body of Pappu was got conducted after which, the body was handed over to his relatives. Thereafter, IO got to know about the ownership of the Tractor and served the notice u/s. 133 MV Act upon the owner of the offending vehicle. Owner produced the driver of the offending vehicle. Driver was arrested and was released on bail as the offence was bailable. Mechanical inspection of offending vehicle was got conducted and released on Superdari. Documents pertaining to the offending vehicle were got verified and they were found to be correct. Thereafter, IO submitted the MLC of the injured Ajay for final opinion and later, he collected the same. As per final opinion of MLC, the injury was 'simple'. On completion of investigation, chargesheet was filed against respondent no. 1, Sanjay Kachhi under Section 279/337/304A IPC and DAR was filed before this Tribunal. Written statements: 5. Respondent nos. 1 and 2 did not file any written statement. Respondent no. 3 filed its reply. ISSUES FRAMED 6. On the basis of the pleading of the parties, vide order dated 31.10.2023, this Tribunal had framed the following issues: Ajay (I)(Fir414/2019/Burari) vs Sanjay Kachhi (Oic) on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172781374/ 2 i. Relief. EVIDENCE 7. The petitioner examined himself as PW-1. Respondent no. 3 examined Ms. Bharti Meena, Deputy Manager, Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. As R3W1. 8. The petitioners had filed Form XIV. Financial statement of the petitioner was recorded and final arguments were heard on behalf of the petitioner and respondent no. 3. In this matter, to prove the occurrence of the accident, the petitioner examined himself as PW-1 who deposed as under: "1. That after the said accident, the deponent and deceased Pappu Bansal were taken into TSR and admitted to LNJP hospital, New Delhi. The deponent was treated at LNJP Hospital, New Delhi and MLC bearing no. 113692859/2019 was prepared by the attending doctors, which clearly indicates the grievous injuries left elbow and left wrist. 5 That the deponent is suffering with intolerable pain and agony, during the entire periods of treatment from the above said hospital. 6. That the deponent is earning livelihood for his family members and at the time of his accident, he sustained grievous injuries left elbow and left wrist and abrasion etc. and during the period of treatment in the hospital, his family members have to face tremendous harassment and mental pain and agony and the treatment of the deponent is still continues and subsists. 7. That the respondent no. 1 is the driver of offending vehicle bearing No. HR 55G 3251 (tractor), who was driving the offending vehicle in a very most rash, negligent, Ajay (I)(Fir414/2019/Burari) vs Sanjay Kachhi (Oic) on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172781374/ 4 reckless and zig-zag manner at a very high speed without any regard from the traffic rules or any concern for human safety. The respondent no. 2 is the owner of the offending vehicle bearing No. HR55G 3251 and the respondent no. 3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing no. HR 55G 3151 (tractor) hence, all the respondents are jointly and severally liable to compensate the deponent/injured for his better treatment. Occupationally, the deponent/injured at the time of accident, the deponent was working as Beldar and earning for a sum of Rs. 20,000/- per month from the said work. But due to heavy impact, the entire activity of the deponent has come to standstill because the work of the deponent was beldari. Disfiguration: 26. Therefore, it is held that the petitioner shall be entitled to interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of DAR i.e. 16.01.2021 till realization. DISBURSEMENT 29. The Financial Statement of petitioner/injured was recorded by this Court/Tribunal. As per the said statement, the monthly expenses of his family are approximately Rs.15,000/- per month. 5. Total Compensation Rs. 27,950/- 6. Interest awarded 6% 7. Interest amount upto the date Rs. 6,121.05/- of award (03 years 07 months (rounded off to Rs. 6,121/-) and 08 days ) 8. Award amount released As mentioned in para no. 29 10. Award amount kept in FDRs N/A. 11. Mode of disbursement of the As mentioned in para no. 29 award amount of the claimant(s) 12. Next date for compliance of 09.10.2024 the award LIABILITY: 33. The offending vehicle was being driven by respondent no.1 Sanjay, owned by respondent no. 2, Vichitra Construction and insured with respondent no. 3, Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. 34.
texts.arguments: Further, procedural approach adopted by an accident claims' tribunal mirrors that of a civil court (National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2009 ACJ 287). In Bimla Devi & Ors. v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors (2009) 13 SC 530, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India that negligence must be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view must be adopted in reaching a conclusion. APP. 690/2017 & CM APPL. 28108/2017, titled as Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs Mona & Ors., date of decision 15.10.2019, which had relied upon the judgment in the case of Cholamandalam Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs Kamlesh 2009(3) AD Delhi 310.) 14. Furthermore, in view of filing of DAR containing the chargesheet for the offences u/s 279/337/304A IPC and other relevant documents against respondent no. 1 and in terms of the judgment in the case of National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, respondent no. 1 Sanjay Kanchi (driver of the offending vehicle) is held to be negligent on the basis of preponderance of probabilities. Therefore, in the absence of any additional evidence, it is held that the petitioner Ajay suffered Ajay (I)(Fir414/2019/Burari) vs Sanjay Kachhi (Oic) on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172781374/ 6 simple injury in the accident in question. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom? Before proceeding further to decide the present issue, it would be apposite to encapsulate the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its guiding lamp post judgment for ascertaining just compensation in road vehicular injury cases. In the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors. (2011) 1 SCC 34, Hon'ble Supreme Court held as under: "General principles relating to compensation in injury cases 4. The provision of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (`Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The Court or tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. (See C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1) SCC 551 and Baker vs. Willoughby Ajay (I)(Fir414/2019/Burari) vs Sanjay Kachhi (Oic) on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172781374/ 7 - 1970 AC 467). 5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following : Pecuniary damages (Special Damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising : (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). The petitioner has claimed Rs. 10,000/- under the head conveyance charges but there is no cogent evidence for the same. Ld. Counsel for respondent no.3 pointed out that the policy in question was a liability only policy that did not cover the risk of extra passengers. It is also their case that while the policy allowed only one person i.e. the driver to sit in the offending vehicle, the facts of the case reveal that the deceased Pappu as well as the injured Ajay were standing on the mudguard thus, violating the terms of the insurance policy. Ld. Counsel for respondent no. 3 argued that since the injured was traveling in the offending vehicle as a gratuitous passenger, the liability cannot be fastened upon the insurance company. He has also submitted that Respondent nos. 1 & 2 were also served with the notice issued under Order 12 Rule 8 CPC to produce the original insurance policy of the offending vehicle covering the category of the vehicle as on the date of accident but the same was never produced before it or before this Tribunal. Ld. Counsel for respondent no. 3/Insurance Company examined Ms. Bharti Meena Deputy Manager, Oriental Insurance Co. as R3W1 who proved the dispatch of notice under Order 12 Rule 8 CPC to respondent nos. 1 & 2. 35. On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for the petitioners argued that the injured was not a gratuitous passenger and the risk with respect to him is, thus, covered in the insurance policy. She further submitted that the insurance company cannot evade liability only on the ground that there were more number of passengers than allowed. 36. From the above arguments of Ld. Counsels for the petitioner and respondent no.3, it is clear that there were more persons than authorized on the offending vehicle. Further, the insurance policy is clear that it allowed a seating capacity of only one person. Therefore, the respondents were in clear violation of the insurance policy and even the injured was a gratuitous passenger who had willingly stood on the mudguard of the offending vehicle knowing the risk it carries with it. The law is well settled that gratuitous passengers are not covered and the insurance company is not liable to indemnify the respondents. Therefore, in the present case, the insurance company is not liable to pay the award amount.
